thread:
incident-bot: PAGER: High 5xx rate (ALB) in eu-central-1 starting ~10m ago. Alert group: infra-prod-alb-5xx. Threshold breached: 15% 5xx over sustained 5m window.

irene (oncall): Ack. seeing spike in Grafana too. dashboards -> prod -> ingress -> alb-eu-central-1.

sam (sre): grabbing logs + target group health. can someone confirm if any deploys in last 30m?

leo (neteng): I don't see deploys from CI, no recent ASG updates. Net metrics show increased retransmits in eu-central-1c.

maya (support): customers on EU region reporting "service errors" via support channel. I have two SEV2 tickets so far. No billing impact yet but UX is broken.

irene (oncall): quick impact check: from kpis, 13% of requests in eu-central-1 are 5xx, traffic level ~70% of normal. Affected endpoints: /api/generate and /v1/chat. TL;DR: partial regional outage for ELB-backed endpoints.

sam (sre): running these checks now:
```bash
# check ALB target health counts
aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn $TG_INGRESS_EU | jq -r '.TargetHealthDescriptions[] | {Id:.Target.Id, State:.TargetHealth.State, Reason:.TargetHealth.Reason}'

# check instance status in eu-central-1
aws ec2 describe-instance-status --region eu-central-1 --filters Name=instance-state-name,Values=running
```

sam (sre): target group shows ~18% unhealthy, mostly in eu-central-1b. Instances are running but app logs show repeated errno 104 connection resets and frequent EBS write stalls on a subset of nodes.

leo (neteng): that maps to the retransmit spike — possibly ENI/host networking or AWS fabric in 1b. I'm seeing higher packet drops on some ENIs from our VPC flow logs.

incident-bot: aws-support-bot created case #1234567890 with AWS Support (severity: high). Case link: https://console.aws.amazon.com/support/cases#/case/?caseId=1234567890

irene (oncall): Init mitigation plan:
- Step 1: Reduce customer impact ASAP: shift Route53 weights away from eu-central-1 to eu-west-1 as failover / partial traffic shift.
- Step 2: Drain unhealthy targets in problematic AZ, scale up ASG in eu-central-1a/c where healthy.
- Step 3: Engage AWS (case opened), attach diagnostic bundles.
- Step 4: Prepare external status update and notify support to message affected customers.

sam (sre): On Step 2: running drain on targets in 1b now. Command:
```bash
aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn $TG_INGRESS_EU --targets Id=i-0abcd1234efgh5678
```
Also increasing desired capacity + adding warm instances to eu-central-1a,c with a smaller instance type to keep capacity but reduce EBS pressure.

leo (neteng): Route53 change ready. Suggest weighted routing with 0.8 weight to eu-west-1 and 0.2 to eu-central-1 to reduce blast radius while keeping some traffic for health checks. I'll push the change and monitor.

irene (oncall): Do it. Also enable Route53 failover health check TTL low (30s). Command snippet for reference:
```bash
# change record set (JSON payload) to adjust weight/failover
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z123456 --change-batch file://shift-weight-eu.json
```

maya (support): Drafting status page note: "We are experiencing elevated errors for customers routed to eu-central-1. We are shifting traffic to eu-west-1 and monitoring. No action required from customers." Shall I post now or wait 10m?

irene (oncall): Post now with 'investigating' and note mitigations in progress. Track update cadence every 15 minutes.

incident-bot: irene (oncall) set incident severity -> P1, pager escalations enabled.

sam (sre): After draining 1b targets and adding 6 new instances, 5xx dropped to ~6% in eu-central-1 within 4 minutes. Overall eu region 5xx now ~3.2%. Still monitoring for flapping.

leo (neteng): Route53 change propagated, initial telemetry shows ~65% traffic rerouted to eu-west-1 within first minute. Health checks still green for eu-west-1.

aws-support-bot: AWS Support replied: "Investigating networking fabric in eu-central-1b; possible EBS backend IO degradation impacting EC2 instances. We'll provide updates within 30 minutes."

sam (sre): collecting diagnostic bundles (sar, dmesg, iostat, cloudwatch logs) and uploading to AWS case. Command used:
```bash
# bundle upload snippet
aws s3 cp diagnostics.tar.gz s3://redwood-diagnostics/1725012345/ && aws support add-attachments-to-case --case-id 1234567890 --attachments file://attachment-meta.json --region us-east-1
```

maya (support): Noted—two large customers requested immediate RTO estimate. We gave interim message: "Traffic is being shifted and mitigations are working; expected improvement over next 30–60 minutes. We will provide updates every 15 minutes."

irene (oncall): Handoff: I'm on call for next 20 minutes then handing to sam for continuation. Sam, if AWS indicates fabric fix, keep a dial with AWS SC; if not, we may escalate to account team.

sam (sre): Ack. Taking over. I'll coordinate with leo and AWS. Leaving a checkpoint: current status:
- 5xx eu-central-1: 5.8% (down from 15%)
- Traffic shifted: ~70% now in eu-west-1
- ASG scaled: +6 instances (eu-central-1a/c)
- Case #1234567890 open with AWS (high severity)

leo (neteng): continuing to watch ENI retransmits. If we see recurrence, plan B is to update ALB to cross-zone load balancing off/on toggle or create a new ALB in eu-west-1 and cut over (short TTL). Will prepare playbook.

aws-support-bot: AWS update: "Root cause being investigated: EBS control plane experiencing throttling in eu-central-1b correlated with host-level spikes. Recommend keeping instances drained in 1b and AWS will remediate host-side resource contention."

maya (support): published status page update and emailed affected customers with note and ETA ~60m. No major revenue-impacting customers declared SEV1 yet.

sam (sre): marking this thread for follow-up postmortem. I'll capture timeline, mitigations, and config changes (Route53 weights, drained targets, ASG scale, diagnostic artifacts).

irene (oncall): handing complete. Thanks team. I'll join postmortem.

incident-bot: incident mitigation actions logged to incident tracker: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2024-0456

leo (neteng): staying on watch for 2h. If AWS completes remediation on their hosts, we'll gradually shift traffic back and reintroduce drained instances after validation.

sam (sre): last note: remember to revert Route53 TTL/weights only after monitoring for 30m of stable 5xx <1% and target health >99%.

maya (support): closing support thread when customers confirm service restored. Will update postmortem with impacted ticket ids.

incident-bot: Thread closed for now (auto). If errors spike again, re-open or @here to re-escalate.
